title: Reconcile Helios leases, approved power, deferred revenue, and loan draws
prompt: Build the Helios project-state and future-cash-flow view at the cutoff. Keep critical IT load separate from gross approved power, phase delivery separately from executed leases, advance billings separately from earned revenue, and an up-to facility separately from funded debt. Evaluate every candidate action and claim against all controlling evidence and include only labels consistent with every relevant clause. Report only.

observations.content: Three executed lease phases cover 133 MW, 260 MW, and 133 MW of critical IT load under approximately 15-year terms, totaling 526 MW. The initial 133 MW retrofit is expected in phases by the end of the first half of 2026; the additional phases are expected to begin delivery in 2027 and reach the contracted total by 2028.

The initial critical IT phase uses about 200 MW of gross power, and 600 MW of gross power supports the later 393 MW of critical IT load. Beyond that 800 MW, another 830 MW of ERCOT-approved gross power remained available to be contracted. Approval does not itself make that remainder contracted, delivered, or revenue-producing.

The data-center segment had $150 million of lease billings received in advance and recorded as deferred lease revenue. It recognized no data-center lease revenue during 2025 and expected revenue only as delivery of critical IT load begins.

A senior secured term facility provides up to $1.4 billion to finance the first phase and related project costs. $878 million was outstanding at year end; the facility maximum is not the same as cash drawn.

The project borrower must maintain a maximum 80% loan-to-cost ratio until stabilization. A minimum 1.40 debt-service coverage ratio begins with the first full quarter after stabilization, alongside restrictions on debt, liens, investments, affiliate transactions, fundamental changes, and misuse of funds.

oracle.terminal_when: The report phases critical IT delivery and revenue, excludes approved-but-uncontracted gross power from backlog, preserves deferred billings, and distinguishes facility capacity from actual draws and triggered covenants.

title: Separate Lake Mariner lease execution from commencement and durable site control
prompt: Build the Lake Mariner agreement-state and cash-flow view at the cutoff. Reconcile four signed customer leases with lease-by-lease commencement, prepaid rent, additional-work conditions, leasehold land, improvement reversion, operating critical IT, and conditional expansion. Evaluate every candidate action and claim against all controlling evidence and include only labels consistent with every relevant clause. Report only.

observations.content: Four long-term customer HPC leases were executed in December 2024. Two commenced in July and August 2025; the other two were expected to begin in early 2026. Each lease has an initial 10-year term and two five-year renewal options.

August 2025 change orders added work, adjusted base rent, and made the 10-year term commence when specified additional work is achieved. Execution alone therefore does not establish commencement for every lease.

The customer paid $90 million representing the first 12 months of base rent across the leases. Starting at each lease's own commencement, the prepayment offsets 50% of monthly base rent until exhausted. At year end, $58.2 million was current deferred rent and $23.3 million was noncurrent deferred rent.

Restructured related-party ground leases cover 162.7 acres, have an initial 35-year term, and can renew for up to nine additional five-year periods unless timely termination notice is given. Buildings and improvements revert to the lessor at expiration; the campus operator does not own the land and improvements in perpetuity.

The campus had 18 critical IT MW of operating HPC capacity. It was undergoing phased expansion toward approximately 500 gross MW in the near term and potentially 750 gross MW subject to additional grid approvals. The lease restructuring grants access to power and infrastructure up to 750 MW, which is not evidence that 750 MW is operating.

oracle.terminal_when: The report recognizes rent by actual lease commencement, preserves the deferred prepayment, and distinguishes leasehold control and conditional gross-power access from operating critical IT capacity.

title: Interpret Tydal open-book construction economics, governance, and risk allocation
prompt: Build the Tydal AI conversion agreement-state view at the cutoff. Distinguish an estimate from a fixed price, indicative dates from binding milestones, cost-plus remuneration from equipment pass-throughs, owner approval from contractor risk, and payment protection from project financing. Evaluate every candidate action and claim against all controlling evidence and include only labels consistent with every relevant clause. Report only.

observations.content: An executed design-and-construction agreement covers conversion of an existing mining data center into an AI data center. Total refurbishment across contractor and external scope is estimated at approximately NOK 4.5 billion excluding VAT. The collaborative implementation is open-book cost-plus, not a disclosed fixed-price cap.

A joint project group decides evolving equipment, technical solutions, interfaces, milestones, and decision plans. The stated December 31, 2026 completion date and other dates remain indicative until determined by that group. Deadlines carry a milestone bonus structure but no daily delay penalties.

Project accounts are due by the 10th of each month, and the project group approves costs for the coming month. A cost more than 10% above the original decision goes back for approval or rejection. The owner can audit remuneration and supply-chain records through December 31, 2030; audit cost shifts to the contractor if material nonconformities are found.

Equipment is bought in the contractor's or owner's name and passed through without markup. The contractor prepares competitive procurement support and follows the project group's decision, but does not bear delay, defect, or failure risk caused by equipment faults; it must pursue the supplier complaint for the owner.

The contractor invoices monthly in arrears after account review, with payment structured to keep it cash neutral rather than financing project costs. If an undisputed invoice remains unpaid after its due date and seven days following written notice, the contractor may suspend work and claim documented time and cost effects.

The site remained an existing data center being converted for colocation use, with planning, design, decommissioning, and long-lead equipment activity underway. Its 50 MW first phase and 175 MW second phase describe site capacity, not proof of completed AI delivery under the new agreement.

oracle.terminal_when: The report preserves open-book governance, treats cost and schedule as controlled but not fixed, allocates equipment and payment risk according to the agreement, and does not turn existing site capacity into completed AI delivery.
